{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 70,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Global group manage check treats VIEW as MANAGE",
      "body": "GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. This global check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() through auth.groups().requireManage(), so a caller who only has 'view' on Groups can create top-level groups. The manage check should evaluate only the MANAGE scope."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 121,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type",
      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates individual resources for groups, users, and clients with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() later looks up group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Because individual group resources have no type, that query only finds the type-level 'Groups' resource and misses all per-group resources, breaking group-restricted user queries and counts."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 123,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs",
      "body": "In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code evaluates and stores groupResource.getId(). For V2 group resources, the actual group ID is the resource name, not the authorization resource ID. The returned set is later used as group IDs for user search/count filtering (UserModel.GROUPS), so filtering is done with internal authorization IDs, and may also include the 'Groups' type resource. This makes group-based user search restrictions, pagination, and user counts incorrect. The method should use the resource name as the group ID, skip the type-level resource, and handle all-groups permissions explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java",
      "line": 94,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Group removal listener is not V2-aware and can throw UnsupportedOperationException",
      "body": "AdminPermissions.registerListener() registers a GroupRemovedEvent listener that calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When V2 admin permissions are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException. Depending on feature configuration, this can either make group deletion fail with an exception or leave V2 authorization resources orphaned. The listener needs V2-aware cleanup or a safe no-op."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java",
      "line": 326,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Group management/permissions endpoints can return 500 under V2",
      "body": "GroupResource.getManagementPermissions() calls permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group), and the corresponding PUT endpoint calls setPermissionsEnabled(). GroupPermissionsV2 implements these methods by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. If the V2 feature is active and the V1 feature gate allows the endpoint, requests to /groups/{id}/management/permissions will fail with HTTP 500 instead of returning a safe disabled state or a proper unsupported response."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 71,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Impersonation evaluation uses the target user's identity when a requester client is provided",
      "body": "UserPermissionsV2.canImpersonate(UserModel user, ClientModel requester) builds a DefaultEvaluationContext with UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the identity of the user being impersonated, and then evaluates the IMPERSONATE scope. This means the caller/requester identity is not used for the permission evaluation when a requester client is present. Policies granting the calling client or admin the right to impersonate may not match, while policies tied to the target user may control the result. canClientImpersonate() delegates to this method, so client-initiated impersonation authorization is likely incorrect."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java",
      "line": 157,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Group count endpoint ignores fine-grained group permissions",
      "body": "GroupsResource.getGroupCount() only calls requireList() and then returns realm-wide group counts via getGroupsCountByNameContaining() or getGroupsCount(). Because canList() can be true through QUERY_GROUPS while GET /groups is filtered by canView(group), a caller who cannot view any groups can still learn the total number of groups and the number of groups matching a search string. The count should be filtered using the same permissions as the group listing."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 238,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "NullPointerException in getScope for missing or unknown resource type",
      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or present in the map. A request creating or updating a scope permission with a missing/invalid resource type can therefore cause a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 147,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Possible NullPointerException when the all-groups resource is missing",
      "body": "GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) when a specific group resource is not found, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the schema is not supported or the type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission()."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 121,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Group permission lookup evaluates every group resource on user searches",
      "body": "GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates over all Group resources and performs a full policy evaluation for each one. This method is invoked by user search/count endpoints such as UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource whenever the caller lacks global user view permission. In realms with many groups, every restricted user search can trigger O(number of groups) authorization evaluations, which may be very slow."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 334,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Group resource names are not resolved for display",
      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only resolves resource names for the Users resource type. For Groups resources it returns resource.getDisplayName(), but individual group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. As a result, authorization policy UIs or representations may show an empty or meaningless identifier instead of the group name/path. A GROUPS case should resolve the group and return a useful name."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Global group manage check treats VIEW as MANAGE
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. This global check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() through auth.groups().requireManage(), so a caller who only has 'view' on Groups can create top-level groups. The manage check should evaluate only the MANAGE scope.

findings.title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates individual resources for groups, users, and clients with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() later looks up group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Because individual group resources have no type, that query only finds the type-level 'Groups' resource and misses all per-group resources, breaking group-restricted user queries and counts.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code evaluates and stores groupResource.getId(). For V2 group resources, the actual group ID is the resource name, not the authorization resource ID. The returned set is later used as group IDs for user search/count filtering (UserModel.GROUPS), so filtering is done with internal authorization IDs, and may also include the 'Groups' type resource. This makes group-based user search restrictions, pagination, and user counts incorrect. The method should use the resource name as the group ID, skip the type-level resource, and handle all-groups permissions explicitly.

findings.title: Group removal listener is not V2-aware and can throw UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() registers a GroupRemovedEvent listener that calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When V2 admin permissions are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException. Depending on feature configuration, this can either make group deletion fail with an exception or leave V2 authorization resources orphaned. The listener needs V2-aware cleanup or a safe no-op.

findings.title: Group management/permissions endpoints can return 500 under V2
findings.body: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions() calls permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group), and the corresponding PUT endpoint calls setPermissionsEnabled(). GroupPermissionsV2 implements these methods by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. If the V2 feature is active and the V1 feature gate allows the endpoint, requests to /groups/{id}/management/permissions will fail with HTTP 500 instead of returning a safe disabled state or a proper unsupported response.

findings.title: Impersonation evaluation uses the target user's identity when a requester client is provided
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.canImpersonate(UserModel user, ClientModel requester) builds a DefaultEvaluationContext with UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the identity of the user being impersonated, and then evaluates the IMPERSONATE scope. This means the caller/requester identity is not used for the permission evaluation when a requester client is present. Policies granting the calling client or admin the right to impersonate may not match, while policies tied to the target user may control the result. canClientImpersonate() delegates to this method, so client-initiated impersonation authorization is likely incorrect.

findings.title: Group count endpoint ignores fine-grained group permissions
findings.body: GroupsResource.getGroupCount() only calls requireList() and then returns realm-wide group counts via getGroupsCountByNameContaining() or getGroupsCount(). Because canList() can be true through QUERY_GROUPS while GET /groups is filtered by canView(group), a caller who cannot view any groups can still learn the total number of groups and the number of groups matching a search string. The count should be filtered using the same permissions as the group listing.

findings.title: NullPointerException in getScope for missing or unknown resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or present in the map. A request creating or updating a scope permission with a missing/invalid resource type can therefore cause a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) when a specific group resource is not found, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the schema is not supported or the type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission().

findings.title: Group permission lookup evaluates every group resource on user searches
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates over all Group resources and performs a full policy evaluation for each one. This method is invoked by user search/count endpoints such as UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource whenever the caller lacks global user view permission. In realms with many groups, every restricted user search can trigger O(number of groups) authorization evaluations, which may be very slow.

findings.title: Group resource names are not resolved for display
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only resolves resource names for the Users resource type. For Groups resources it returns resource.getDisplayName(), but individual group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. As a result, authorization policy UIs or representations may show an empty or meaningless identifier instead of the group name/path. A GROUPS case should resolve the group and return a useful name.
